key_insight: Free-stream forcing triggers non-modal perturbations in hypersonic blunt-body boundary layers through a two-stage mechanism: slow-down convection near the nose boosts streamwise vorticity by O(√R), then lift-up downstream amplifies streamwise velocity up to O(R).
engineering_relevance: These receptivity mechanisms help predict and control disturbance growth in hypersonic boundary layers, which is important for transition, heating, and vehicle design.
method: High-Reynolds-number asymptotic analysis of the receptivity process
Physical decomposition into nose-region slow-down convection and downstream lift-up
Reduced-order model for downstream evolution of non-modal perturbations
evidence_signal: The reduced model is validated against SF-HLNS calculations and shows good agreement across the studied parameter range.
watch_item: The asymptotic reduced model is derived for high-Reynolds-number blunt-body boundary layers, so accuracy may drop outside the assumed regime or for strongly different wall-temperature/nose-radius conditions.
paper_title: Excitation of non-modal perturbations in hypersonic boundary layers by free stream forcing. Part II: asymptotic theory and key mechanisms
